questions.q: Describe the main features of Mauryan art, especially the Ashokan pillars.
answer: Mauryan art, at its height under Ashoka, was monumental and closely linked to the state and to Buddhism.

answer.text: The most striking works are the Ashokan pillars, tall monolithic columns of sandstone carrying the emperor's edicts. They are famous for their extraordinary smooth shine, known as the Mauryan polish. Each pillar has a shaft, a capital and an animal figure on top.

The finest is the Lion Capital at Sarnath, with four lions standing back to back above a wheel and figures of animals. It has been adopted as the National Emblem of India, and the wheel appears on the National Flag.
Popular art included large yaksha and yakshi statues such as the Didarganj Yakshi, while rock-cut caves like those at Barabar and the core of the Sanchi Stupa also belong to this age.

answer: Thus Mauryan art combined grandeur with fine craftsmanship.
